title: A Neuroprosthetic SoC Featuring Rapid Local Sensory Feedback with On-Chip Unsupervised Multi-Class Spike Sorting
summary: This letter presents a 65 nm neuroprosthetic system-on-chip (SoC) featuring a rapid feedback pathway from motor recording to sensory stimulation. To enable low-latency sensory mapping modulated by individual-neuron firing rates, the SoC integrates a mixed-signal unsupervised spike-sorting module with stimulation-artifact rejection, a programmable sliding-window firing-rate calculator, and a closed-loop controller for adapting stimulation parameters. The spike-sorting module combines event-driven analog feature extraction with Manhattan-distance-based digital clustering while consuming 1.6 $\mu$W/channel. On the Quiroga Difficult-1 benchmark, it achieves 94.58% three-class accuracy, with only a 0.4% reduction when stimulation artifacts are introduced at 20% of the spike count. The closed-loop controller supports polynomial and logarithmic mapping functions and incorporates Mitchell's approximation for power saving. The SoC is fully characterized on the bench and in vivo.

title: Mission Capability-Aware UAV Swarm Coordination for Autonomous Disaster Response
summary: This paper proposes an artificial intelligence (AI) driven mission capability aware unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarm coordination framework for autonomous post disaster search and rescue. An integrated sensing and communication enabled master high altitude platform station senses the disaster environment, detects victims and hazards, and constructs adaptive rescue regions based on spatially varying mission demands. A mission capability requirement (MCR) quantifies regional capability demand, while a normalized mission capability score (MCS) characterizes the real time capability of individual UAVs. A capability-aware assignment mechanism matches UAV capabilities to regional requirements while minimizing deployment distance. An MCS based reallocation mechanism dynamically transfers UAVs from capability surplus to capability deficient regions while preserving donor sufficiency. A hierarchical deep reinforcement learning framework with proximal policy optimization performs high-level region selection, while MCR MCS matching enables feasible UAV level reallocation. Finally, joint trajectory optimization considers travel time, distance, propulsion energy, operational capability, obstacle avoidance, and inter UAV collision avoidance. Theoretical analysis and simulations demonstrate improved mission capability satisfaction, resource efficiency, and disaster response performance

title: A new class of optimal binary linear complementary pairs of codes
summary: The construction of optimal binary linear complementary pair (LCP) has recently attracted considerable attention in coding theory. Based on the Belov codes, this paper proposes a novel construction of optimal binary LCPs with $\theta=4$, extending our previous work on $\theta=3$. Our results not only yield abundant new optimal binary LCPs with flexible parameters, but also enable more optimal binary LCPs with smaller minimum distances.

title: Data-Driven Spectrum Access Technologies for 6G
summary: The surge in global mobile traffic, driven by 5G adoption and emerging applications, necessitates new spectrum allocations for 6G systems. With most major swaths of spectrum below 15 GHz already allocated to other services, co-existence between cellular and incumbent services such as satellite or radar systems is critical to make such spectrum accessible for 6G. At the same time, the advent of artificial intelligence offers a new opportunity for designing more efficient spectrum sharing techniques. This paper presents four novel data-driven spectrum access techniques to enable efficient use of spectrum for the 6G era: 1) co-existence technique for efficient protection of fixed incumbent receivers within an established protection area; 2) data-driven approach for protecting satellite receivers via control of radiated power above the horizon; 3) spectrum sensing-based fast-time-scale physical resource block blanking; and 4) base station-based spectrum occupancy detection to enable fast-time-scale spectrum sharing with satellite and non-terrestrial network incumbents. These techniques leverage artificial intelligence and extreme multiple-input multiple-output capabilities to enable efficient spectrum co-existence/sharing while maintaining cellular network performance.

title: Beyond TR 38.811 for 6G NTN Channel Models
summary: As the 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) expands 6G non-terrestrial network (NTN) to S, Ku, and Ka bands for integration with existing terrestrial cellular networks, the necessary satellite channel model for link and network performance evaluation remains tied to TR 38.811, last revised in 2020. We identify issues on multiple fronts: inappropriate parameter specifications based on very limited site-specific environments considered, omission of satellite-induced Doppler spread and directional antenna effects and lack of a transparent channel model generation procedure. To address these limitations, we re-derive the channel parameters using ray tracing (RT) over urban and rural environments based on ITU-R building statistics. Our results show that TR 38.811 substantially overestimates the K-factor at low elevations and predicts a decreasing trend with elevation, which is inconsistent with RT. The Ka-band clutter loss (CL) also exceeds the RT estimates by more than 15 dB in urban cases. It also underestimates rural delay spread (DS) at low elevations and predicts an elevation trend inconsistent with RT. We further quantify the previously neglected satellite-induced Doppler spread. Finally, we demonstrate that the conventional TR 38.811 channel generator significantly underestimates the K-factor in the presence of directional antenna (beamforming), while our modified generator substantially reduces this discrepancy.

title: Timely Ground-Station Status Delivery via UAV-Assisted Data Collection and Hierarchical RL
summary: We consider a UAV-assisted status-update system in which a rotary-wing unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) collects updates from multiple sensors, stores the newest update of each sensor, and forwards selected buffered updates to a ground station (GS). We minimize a weighted sum of the time-average GS-side age of information (AoI) and UAV energy consumption over a finite horizon. The optimization is subject to half-duplex operation, sensor and UAV energy-causality constraints, transmission-rate and power limits, and a terminal-location constraint. Because collection changes the information age at the UAV but does not reduce the GS-side AoI until the buffered update is forwarded, mobility, collection, and forwarding decisions are coupled over time. We use a hierarchical AoI-energy actor-critic (HAE-AC) controller in which a coarse-timescale actor selects return-feasible UAV movements, while a deterministic per-slot scheduler constructs feasible collection or forwarding sets and assigns the minimum transmit power required for each scheduled transmission. In a 100-sensor deployment, HAE-AC reduces the average GS-side AoI by about 22% relative to an adaptive staleness-gated benchmark. Compared with forward-upon-collection, selective buffered forwarding reduces the number of downlink bursts by roughly 30% while increasing the number of collections per sensor by more than 23%.

title: GTAC: A Graph-Transformer Actor-Critic for Carrier-Aware MU-MIMO User Grouping
summary: Achieving higher spectral efficiency (SE) in 5G and future 6G networks requires efficient massive multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) grouping under coupled physical-layer constraints and strict scheduling deadlines. Motivated by industry efforts in AI-native RAN, we propose Graph-Transformer Actor-Critic (GTAC), a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) architecture for carrier-aware MU-MIMO user grouping. The objective is to maximize the long-term proportional-fair (PF) utility of the cell subject to constraints from the practical stack protocol. GTAC comprises a shared actor--critic encoder with spatial-edge-biased attention mechanism, a pointer decoder actor that generates grouping decisions, and a multi-stage transformer critic that estimates the carrier-wide state-value during training. Training begins by cloning a teacher policy that cannot meet real-time deployment deadlines, followed by critic warmup and two-stage reinforcement learning using proximal policy optimization (PPO), first on a narrow, power-matched carrier and then on the full carrier with a Kullback--Leibler (KL) policy anchor. After two-stage PPO, the best GTAC policy outperforms the non-real-time teacher by 11.6% in carrier SE, while exceeding its PF utility and preserving the cell-edge throughput. A CUDA implementation of GTAC achieves a 69.6 us inference latency on an RTX PRO 4500 GPU, below the targeted 100 us inference budget in practical systems.

title: RFShape: An IQ-Pretrained Wireless Foundation Model for Heterogeneous IQ & CIR Representations
summary: In wireless systems, foundation models have been proposed as alternative artificial intelligence models to replace task-specific models with a shared pretrained model that can be reused across many downstream applications (source separation, interference detection, localization, etc.). These wireless foundation models promise to reuse learned representations across diverse tasks, but choosing a foundation model also means choosing its input representation. For example, a model pretrained on spectrograms expects spectrograms, while one pretrained on in-phase/quadrature (IQ) samples expects IQ, limiting which pretrained model can be used for a given downstream problem. To remedy this, we present RFShape, a 7.4 M-parameter foundation model that breaks this coupling by adapting how a signal is presented to a shared pretrained encoder. RFShape is pretrained solely on synthetic IQ waveforms, without real captures, labels, or channel impulse responses (CIRs), and uses deterministic representation operators to support heterogeneous downstream inputs. Across ten tasks and nine datasets unseen during pretraining, the same encoder supports classification, ranging-error regression, and two-dimensional positioning. Representation selection alone increases 23-class radar recognition from 23.0% to 69.5% and short-range technology recognition from 70.8% to 97.1%. RFShape also outperforms CIR-pretrained ultra-wideband baselines by up to 12.7 percentage points for (N)LOS classification despite never observing CIRs during pretraining. These results show that foundation-model reuse need not be limited by the representation or modality seen during pretraining, and adapting how a signal is presented can extend a single pretrained encoder across heterogeneous wireless tasks.

title: Positioning and Radiation Efficiency Degrees of Freedom in Cascaded Pinching-Antenna Arrays
summary: In a pinching-antenna system (PASS), a single source feeds multiple pinches, resulting in a cascade that couples their radiated powers. A shared radiated-power limit, such as the interference power constraint in an underlay cognitive radio network, couples them again. We study such a network where PASS serves the secondary users. First, we formulate the joint optimization problem of the two degrees of freedom (DoF), pinch positions and radiation efficiencies, and characterize the single-link optimum analytically. Then, rather than proposing one method, we present the results for a grid of schemes whose two axes are the two DoF. Under an order-free attribution, positioning is worth 1.34 times radiation efficiency, and the two are near-perfect substitutes. We also show that substitutability is due to the constraint and not the cascade, since relaxing the constraint by 20 dB removes 97% of their interaction. At the joint reference, not knowing the primary receiver (PR) location costs 6.23 bit/s/Hz, more than twice the 2.87 that optimizing both DoF is worth. Instantaneous fading information adds a further 0.29 bit/s/Hz. Allocating efficiencies at equally spaced positions reaches 98% of the joint reference at about three orders of magnitude less computation.

title: Making Every Edit Count: Efficient Binary Edit Correction at the Gilbert-Varshamov Bound
summary: We construct binary codes that attain the classical Gilbert-Varshamov redundancy guarantee for a fixed number of edit errors, with deterministic polynomial-time construction, encoding, and decoding. For every fixed integer $t\ge 1$ and all sufficiently large block lengths $n$, our codes correct any combination of at most $t$ insertions, deletions, and substitutions in total, with redundancy at most $2t\log_2 n+O_t(1)$. All algorithms run in polynomial time in $n$ for fixed $t$, and decoding recovers the original information message. This realizes the classical counting guarantee algorithmically without enumerating the exponentially large space of binary words.

title: Reconfigurable Antenna-Enhanced ISAC: A Unified Perspective on Electromagnetic Adaptation
summary: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) enables sensing and communication (S&C) functions to share time, frequency, and hardware resources, offering an efficient paradigm for next-generation wireless systems. However, conventional fixed-configuration antenna (FCA) architectures provide limited flexibility in adapting the physical electromagnetic (EM) response of the end-to-end wireless link. This article develops a unified EM-adaptation perspective on reconfigurable antenna (RA)-enhanced ISAC systems. We distinguish transceiver-side (TSc-side) and environment-side (Env-side) RA deployments and identify five fundamental EM reconfiguration dimensions: position, orientation, radiation pattern, polarization, and frequency response. Building on this framework, we examine how these dimensions customize communication channels, actively control target information mapping for sensing, and reshape the interplay between S&C, particularly by improving compatibility between S&C requirements under shared resources. Two case studies illustrate how TSc-side and Env-side EM reconfiguration can improve spatial selectivity and the achievable S&C performance tradeoff. Finally, we discuss several promising directions for advancing RA-enhanced ISAC systems, including fundamental performance limits, low-overhead black-box optimization, and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled semantic ISAC.

title: Hardware-Efficient Reinforcement-Learned Scheduling for Quantum LDPC Decoders
summary: Quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes are promising for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but their decoding algorithms present significant hardware implementation challenges. Reinforcement-learned sequential belief propagation (RL-S) improves the error-correction performance of conventional belief propagation (BP) through adaptive variable-node scheduling. However, its heap-based priority management introduces substantial hardware overhead. This paper presents hardware implementations of BP, RL-S, and bucket-based reinforcement-learned BP (BRL-S) for the [[288,12,18]] bivariate bicycle QLDPC code. The BRL-S architectures employ quantized priorities and first-in, first-out (FIFO) buckets to simplify scheduling. Three configurations with two, four, and eight priority levels are evaluated. FPGA synthesis results demonstrate that BRL-S reduces lookup-table utilization by approximately 68--72% compared with RL-S. ASIC synthesis further shows reductions of 63--67% in area and 64--69% in estimated power consumption. These results demonstrate that bucket-based scheduling substantially improves the hardware efficiency of reinforcement-learned QLDPC decoders.

AI.motivation: 量子LDPC码的强化学习序列化BP（RL-S）虽提升纠错性能，但基于堆的优先级管理带来巨大硬件开销，需要更高效的调度实现。

title: Toward Generalized LEO Channel Prediction: A Rapid Adaptation Time-Frequency Mamba Framework
summary: Accurate channel state information (CSI) prediction is pivotal for enhancing system capacity in low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite-terrestrial communications within the sixth-generation vision of global ubiquitous connectivity. However, the extreme mobility of LEO satellites, coupled with significant propagation delays, induces severe channel aging. Existing deep learning (DL) methods often struggle with non-stationary dynamics or generalize poorly across diverse global geographies. To address these challenges, we design the Evo-TFMamba, which is an evolutionary framework integrating time-frequency selective Mamba blocks with meta-learning for generalized CSI prediction. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed Evo-TFMamba performs adaptive prediction according to the geographic coverage of LEO satellites. Meanwhile, it significantly enhances the model's generalization ability, particularly when faced with unseen channel environments in LEO satellite communication.

title: Optimal Communication for Distributed Sparse Histogram Aggregation
summary: Histogram estimation is a fundamental primitive in distributed data analysis, with applications in counting queries and federated learning. In many settings, the universe of categories is enormous, yet each user's data involves only a small subset, yielding sparse local histograms. This raises a natural question: To what extent can local sparsity reduce the communication needed to estimate the global histogram? We answer this question by characterizing the communication complexity of distributed sparse histogram estimation under prescribed $\ell_1$ distortion and failure probability constraints. Our upper bound is achieved by a randomized covering scheme that optimizes how accurately each user represents its local histogram to reduce communication. By exploiting the distortion budget directly rather than imposing unbiasedness, the scheme achieves lower communication costs than standard unbiased sampling and hashing constructions. We establish the scheme's first-order optimality through a lower bound based on local support identification. The key step is to relate communication cost directly to the number of active coordinates revealed by each user's message, rather than to bound information about the aggregate via distance-based Fano's inequalities. This characterization further quantifies how the communication advantage of heterogeneous over homogeneous encoders varies across parameter regimes.

AI.tldr: 该论文刻画了在ℓ1失真与失败概率约束下分布式稀疏直方图估计的通信复杂度，提出随机覆盖方案达到上界的最优一阶性能。
AI.motivation: 分布式数据分析中类别空间巨大而用户数据稀疏，希望量化局部稀疏性能在多大程度上降低估计全局直方图所需通信量。

title: Pairwise Distortion Distribution with Graph-Based Importance Sampling for Quantization Error and Intrinsic Dimension Estimation
summary: Quantifying the dimensionality of data is a fundamental need in machine learning and signal processing applications such as representation learning, data compression, and inverse problems, where the extrinsic dimension in which the data is presented can be very different from the intrinsic dimension that determines the operational performance. Various concepts, such as Rényi information dimension, rate-distortion dimension, and quantization dimension are useful here. Despite their theoretical significance, estimating these measures are challenging given their asymptotic definitions. Recent research has shown that analyzing the pairwise distortion distribution (PDD) of a data source can provide a tractable lower bound on the distortion of random codebook quantization, from which a tractable notion of intrinsic dimension can be derived. In this paper we extend this line of research in three main ways. First, we develop a related upper bound on distortion of random codebook quantization. Second, we improve the computability of both the lower and upper bounds, using a graph-based adaptive importance sampling approach. Third, we leverage the bounds to define new notions of intrinsic dimension which form upper and lower bounds on the Rényi information dimension, rate-distortion dimension, and quantization dimension, and which can be empirically estimated from unknown data sources. We illustrate the concepts by analyzing several artificial and empirical distributions.

title: Movable Antenna Aided Robust Wireless Transmission: From Model-Based Optimization to Scalable Reinforcement Learning
summary: This paper investigates robust joint antenna positioning and precoding for multiuser movable antenna (MA) systems under imperfect channel state information (CSI). First, we identify the mismatch between the spatial statistics of densely sampled MA channels and the discrete Fourier transform (DFT) basis used for conventional robust precoding. To address this, we develop a novel discrete prolate spheroidal sequence (DPSS)-based a posteriori channel model. By exploiting the spatial covariance structure of MA channels, this model is better suited to modeling MA channel uncertainty. Building on this model, we develop an efficient iterative algorithm for robust joint antenna positioning and precoding to maximize the expected sum rate. By transforming the coupled optimization of antenna positioning and precoding at each iteration into direct comparisons of closed-form scores, we design a low-complexity position replacement scheme that effectively reuses matrix computations across candidate sets. To further improve efficiency and scalability, we exploit the inherent tensor equivariance (TE) of the problem to develop a reinforcement learning framework. To explicitly account for channel uncertainty, we develop novel pairwise user-interaction and CSI-conditioned equivariant attention mechanisms to encode channel statistics and adaptively fuse them with the available CSI. We further introduce distance-biased spatial attention to incorporate the geometry of candidate positions into attention weighting, thereby enhancing spatial feature learning. Simulation results show that the proposed methods improve sum-rate performance while reducing online runtime under imperfect CSI. These methods also achieve near-optimal performance under perfect CSI, closely matching the exhaustive-search method. Moreover, the learning framework generalizes across different numbers of users and MAs without retraining.

title: Estimating the generator of matrix exponential time-series
summary: The achievable precision in estimating the spectrum of a time-series signal that is promised to be sparse in Fourier space deteriorates rapidly as the spectral peaks get closer together, as soon as we introduce noise. Here, we study the related task of generator estimation: estimating the generator of a matrix exponential time-series and its eigenvalues. We obtain rigorous non-asymptotic precision guarantees on genESPRIT, a practical algorithm solving generator estimation, and show that this task can be solved with precision independent of the spectral spacing. The guarantees are complemented by a Cramér--Rao analysis of a relaxation of the problem. In particular, in the case of unitary data with bounded additive noise with effective entrywise variance $\sigma^2$, we show that genESPRIT estimates the associated propagator matrix in Frobenius norm with precision scaling as $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(\sigma NL^{-\frac12})$ in the length of the time-series $L$ and matrix dimension $N$, matching the corresponding spectrum-independent Cramér--Rao standard deviation scaling up to logarithmic factors. We prove that the matching distance error in the spectrum estimated by genESPRIT scales as $\tilde{\mathcal{O}} (\sigma^2 N^3 L^{-1} + \sigma N^{\frac32} L^{-\frac32} )$, which we compare to the lower bound on the corresponding Cramér--Rao bound with the asymptotic standard deviation scaling $\mathcal{O}(\sigma L^{-\frac32})$. These guarantees provide the first rigorous bounds on solving the generator estimation problem. As the matrix exponential time-series can be obtained from linearly independent vector time-series by concatenation, this work opens up a new direction in spectral estimation, which circumvents the problem of crowded spectra, under the additional assumption of linear independence.

title: Mutual-Coupling-Aware Joint Precoding and Antenna Positioning for Movable-Antenna MU-MIMO Systems
summary: Movable antennas (MAs) improve wireless communications by adapting antenna positions to the propagation environment. However, antenna movement also changes the mutual coupling (MC) among elements of the transmit and receive arrays, which affects the performance of MA-enabled systems. In this paper, we investigate MC-aware joint precoding and antenna positioning for a downlink multiuser multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) system with MAs at both the base station and users. We establish an MC-aware system model by combining field-response propagation with a circuit-based representation of the transmit and receive arrays. Based on this model, we formulate a weighted sum-rate (WSR) maximization problem that jointly optimizes multi-stream precoders and antenna positions. The problem is challenging because the precoders and positions are coupled through the propagation channels and position-dependent MC matrices. To address this challenge, we reformulate the problem in the antenna-current domain to to efficiently handle the MC matrices and develop a current-domain weighted minimum mean square error (WMMSE) framework for alternating optimization. Furthermore, we handle the nonconvex position updates within the framework by using majorization--minimization (MM) and solve the resulting convex subproblems with a dedicated conic alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed design improves the WSR over both an MC-aware fixed array and a movable-array design that ignores MC during optimization.

title: System-level performance in massive ISAC networks
summary: We propose a dynamic stochastic geometry framework to model and evaluate large-scale integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) networks. Base stations are distributed according to a homogeneous Poisson point process, while user equipments and sensing objects undergo localised random motion around their serving base station. Full spectrum reuse with a common waveform generates mutual interference that couples the two functionalities. Communication performance is characterised through downlink queues whose service rates are governed by the signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) via the Shannon capacity. Sensing performance is captured by a Kalman filter (KF) whose measurement noise covariance depends on the sensing SINR, yielding a non-classical state-dependent filtering problem. We define system-level performance metrics under the Palm distribution of the base station process and prove the consistency of their empirical estimators. We then prove that, for a typical base station, communication and sensing metrics are associated, so that operating regimes favourable to one functionality tend to benefit the other. The proof combines the monotonicity of the queue and filter recursions in the configuration of interferers with the Harris--FKG inequality for Poisson functionals. We also show that the excess association ratio of the two interference levels decays as the inverse of the network density. Simulations based on a ray-tracing channel model corroborate the analysis.

title: Directional Statistics in Signal Processing: A Geometry Driven Overview of Models, Learning, and Applications
summary: Many signal-processing objects are defined by periodicity, normalization, sign or global-phase ambiguity, basis invariance, or positive-semidefinite constraints and therefore cannot be modeled faithfully in ordinary Euclidean space. This paper develops a geometry driven framework for directional statistics in signal processing, connecting signal representations to their natural manifolds or quotient spaces and to probability models compatible with their invariances. After reviewing instances of directional statistics in the signal processing literature, we review circular, toroidal, spherical, projective, Stiefel, Grassmann, and covariance-valued distributions, emphasizing their statistical assumptions, computational requirements, and dimensional limitations relevant to signal processing. We describe various modeling and estimation strategies, including analytical and gradient-based maximum likelihood, structured low-rank parameterizations, mixtures and hidden Markov models (HMMs), score-based and contrastive estimation, and geometry-aware K-means. To exemplify the consequences of geometry-aware modeling, we study multivariate phase coherence in synthetic data and functional neuroimaging, comparing toroidal phase vectors to projective, Grassmann, and positive-semidefinite representations. We also study speaker separation in a car environment, showing that directional representations outperform a standard Euclidean model. These examples demonstrate that when the geometric representation, statistical distribution, inference method, and computational regime are considered together, they have the potential to lead to improved models across a broad range of signal processing applications.

title: Non-asymptotic Sphere-Packing Bounds for Finite-Blocklength Scalar Gaussian Multiple-Access and Broadcast Channels
summary: This paper investigates non-asymptotic achievable rate regions of Gaussian multiple-access channels (MACs) and broadcast channels (BCs) in the finite-blocklength regime. By employing a proposed volume-uniform random coding (VURC) codebook that distributes codewords uniformly within an $n$-dimensional power sphere, together with successive interference cancellation (SIC) decoding, we derive a closed-form achievability bound, a scheme-specific lower bound on the average error probability, and a fourth-order asymptotic characterization. The proposed SIC achievability bound admits a simple and analytically interpretable closed-form expression, enabling direct performance evaluation without iterative computation. The structure of the proposed SIC asymptotic bound offers a highly extensible framework, allowing advances in single-user finite-blocklength theory to be systematically incorporated into the multiuser setting. Futhermore, to characterize the performance benefit of joint decoding, we further derive numerical and closed-form achievability bounds for the two-user Gaussian MAC under joint nearest-neighbor (JNN) decoding. Numerical results illustrate the performance differences among the proposed SIC and JNN bounds and existing benchmarks.

title: Rate-Distortion-Perception Tradeoff for Vector Gaussian Sources with Limited Common Randomness: Exact Characterization and Approximate Universality
summary: The distortion-rate-common randomness-perception (DRCP) theory characterizes how limited common randomness (CR) improves reconstruction fidelity under perceptual constraints, thereby providing an information-theoretic foundation for generative compression. In this paper, we characterize the DRCP tradeoff for vector Gaussian sources with limited CR under the squared-error distortion measure and the squared Wasserstein-2 perception measure. Specifically, we first establish a generalized reverse waterfilling characterization of globally optimal allocations. Second, we derive an analytical upper bound on the DRCP function through sequential greedy allocation of rate and CR. For fixed rate and CR budgets, the resulting representation is independent of the perception threshold. Finally, we establish its approximate universality through uniform performance guarantees: the achievable distortion exceeds the optimal distortion by at most $2\rho^*\approx0.2897$ times the total source variance, whereas the optimal-to-greedy distortion ratio is at least $\eta^*\approx0.7517$.

title: Construction of New Complete Complementary Codes Using Extended Boolean Functions and Permutations
summary: Complete complementary code (CCC) is a crucial component in the design and optimization of modern wireless communication systems, particularly in addressing challenges related to interference, spectral efficiency, and signal quality. In the literature, CCC constructions are restricted by a set size smaller than the sequence length. In this paper, we introduce a novel construction method for CCCs based on the extended Boolean functions (EBF) that overcome existing restrictions by including a set size bigger than the sequence length. Further, the proposed construction uses functions which are new in literature and provide us with new CCCs. This is also the very first construction where row PMEPR is also bounded by $n$ for a set size in the form of power of $n$.

title: Current-Future Rate Tradeoffs in ISAC Under Random Path Changes
summary: In mobile wireless links, motion changes path directions and visibility, and blockage can shift communication to a different propagation path. Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) allows a base station (BS) to use echoes of data transmissions to monitor these changes and guide subsequent beam selection. Illuminating objects that govern future path availability may reduce the beamforming gain on the current communication route. Existing sensing-communication tradeoffs and dynamic beam-control frameworks do not directly quantify the future communication gain from this current-rate sacrifice. We quantify sensing value by the future-rate gain enabled by echo-adaptive beam selection. We derive explicit expressions for the future communication gain and the net gain after accounting for the current-rate loss. The analysis uses a coupled communication-echo channel with binary-state Markov motion over a finite burst informed by one processed echo. We show that monitoring is worthwhile when its future-rate gain exceeds the current loss, while more informative observations yield zero additional future rate if they cannot change any future optimal beam. We derive interpretable gain bounds exposing the roles of improved scene discrimination, motion memory and future beam-rate differences. Reciprocal-channel tests demonstrate positive net accumulated-rate gains from monitoring a moving blocker during reflected-path service, including continuous position uncertainty.

title: Joint Channel Scanning and Geometry-Aware Codebook Design for Movable Antenna Arrays
summary: Multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems rely on spatial degrees of freedom, but fixed antenna geometries cannot adapt to propagation environments. Movable antenna (MA) systems address this by adapting antenna positions to the channel. In discrete MA architectures, active antennas are selected from candidate positions, requiring channel state information (CSI) at those positions. With limited radio-frequency (RF) chains, CSI is acquired through successive pilot rounds, or antenna scanning, whose overhead can offset reconfiguration gains. This paper studies discrete MA geometry optimization when only a fraction of candidate positions is scanned. We show that a geometry-aware (GA) steering-vector codebook, constructed from the actual antenna coordinates, reconstructs channels more accurately than a conventional discrete Fourier transform (DFT) codebook when the optimized array departs from a uniform grid. We then show that the scanning fraction required to approach full-scan sum-rate performance depends on the CSI acquisition method: least-squares (LS) estimation degrades sharply under sparse scanning, while codebook-based acquisition remains robust. We also propose an adaptive scanning procedure that probes candidates in batches and stops automatically using the acquired pilots, avoiding a preset scanning budget. Finally, we quantify sum-rate losses as users move from their initial positions and evaluate recovery through re-scanning and geometry re-selection, relative to fixed-aperture operation with outdated or fresh CSI. Numerical results show that adaptive scanning achieves about 99.5% of the full-scan sum rate while scanning only 11% of candidate positions.

title: Interpretability Analysis of End-to-End Learned CSI Feedback for Precoding-Oriented Massive MIMO
summary: Recent end-to-end learning frameworks jointly optimize pilot design, channel state information (CSI) feedback, and downlink precoding, achieving strong performance under limited feedback overhead in massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) networks. However, the internal representations and decision-making strategies learned by these architectures remain largely unexplored. This paper presents an interpretability analysis of a precoding-oriented end-to-end CSI feedback framework using explainable artificial intelligence (xAI) techniques. Building on a validated learned architecture, we investigate the structure of the learned pilots, latent feedback representations, and precoding vectors through low-dimensional visualization, density-based clustering, and cross-block representation analysis. The results reveal that the learned system undergoes a transition as the feedback constraint is relaxed. Under stringent feedback budgets, the encoder develops clustered latent representations and quantized precoding behavior. As additional feedback resources become available, the learned representations evolve into smooth geometry-preserving manifolds that retain physically meaningful channel characteristics such as dominant angular information, while enabling more adaptive precoding decisions. Furthermore, the learned pilot signals naturally form complementary sensing patterns aligned with the underlying channel statistics. The analysis also reveals a shift from gain-driven beamforming strategies under severe compression to increasingly interference-aware precoding as the feedback budget increases. These findings provide new insight into how end-to-end learned CSI feedback systems balance compression efficiency and communication performance and establish a general framework for interpreting learned communication architectures.

title: Linear Equivalence of Full Weight Spectrum Cyclic Orbit Codes
summary: We determine the linear-equivalence classes within the two families of full weight spectrum one-orbit cyclic subspace codes. This solves the second open problem posed by Castello, Polverino and Zullo [J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 212 (2025) 106005]. For the first family, the criterion is a fractional linear transformation over $\F_q$ followed by a power of $q$-Frobenius. For the second family, it is an affine transformation over $\F_{q^2}$ together with a power of $q$-Frobenius. We use polynomial spaces over finite fields, the linear-isometry theorem for cyclic orbit codes, and trace duality. The arguments include parameters belonging to proper subfields of the ambient field.

title: Noise Parameter Identification in Ensemble of Atomic Clocks
summary: The paper introduces a parameter identification framework for atomic clock ensembles, where individual clocks are represented by second-order linear stochastic state-space model. The proposed procedure relies exclusively on differential measurements, namely the pairwise phase differences between a designated pivot clock and the remaining ensemble members. The identification targets key parameters for each clock: white and random-walk frequency noise variances, constant frequency drift, and (co)variance of the measurement noise. To identify these parameters, two distinct identification methods are proposed. Their estimation accuracy is rigorously demonstrated via numerical simulations and validated using empirical data from atomic hydrogen maser (AHM) clocks at ESTEC Timing Laboratory.

title: The APN Property of Two Families of functions over $\F_{2^{n}}$ from the Switching Construction
summary: Let $m\geq5$ be odd with $3\nmid m$. Helleseth, Ichanska, and Kaleyski \cite{HIK} conjectured that two norm-perturbed Budaghyan--Helleseth--Kaleyski functions $F_2,F_3$ over $\F_{2^{2m}}$ are APN. In this paper, we prove this conjecture. First, by using the basis $(1,\beta)$ of $\F_{2^{2m}}$ over $\F_{2^m}$, we show that $F_2$ and $F_3$ are EA-equivalent to two functions $\mathcal G_1$ and $\mathcal G_0$, respectively. Their derivatives can be written as two trace equations for a matrix $P\in\mathrm{GL}(2,\F_{2^m})$. We then prove that these two equations have no solution. The proof uses only identities over finite fields, the characteristic polynomial of a $2\times2$ matrix, and elementary properties of Frobenius automorphisms. The repeated-root case and all parity cases are considered separately. It follows that the derivative of each function has kernel of size two in every nonzero direction, and hence both $F_2$ and $F_3$ are APN for every admissible $m$.

AI.motivation: 解决Helleseth、Ichanska与Kaleyski提出的猜想：验证两个扰范数Budaghyan–Helleseth–Kaleyski函数族是否为APN函数，属有限域密码函数理论研究。

AI.conclusion: 该猜想被完全证明；扰动范数构造可为APN函数设计提供新思路，但本文方法为纯代数证明，未涉及通信中的信道建模或AI方法。

title: 6G ISAC Drone Detection: Signal Processing and Experimental Validation at FR1
summary: Integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) enables mobile networks to detect passive targets such as drones at minimal additional cost. However, in ISAC, a small drone must be detected against strong ground clutter with the limited radio resources left by communications. In this paper, we propose two ISAC target detectors: a coherent detector, which combines all frames and beam dwells of a revisit, and a non-coherent detector, robust to inter-frame clock phase drift. The algorithms leverage per-dwell clutter whitening and the adaptive coherence estimator (ACE) detection statistic to improve performance. Both detectors estimate the range, radial velocity, and azimuth of targets in real time on a laptop graphics processing unit (GPU). Measurements with an FR1 ISAC proof-of-concept system based on a commercial base station show that the coherent detector outperforms the non-coherent one and recovers the full track.

title: Rank-metric intersecting codes
summary: Intersecting codes are codes in which any two nonzero codewords share a common nonzero coordinate, and they have been extensively studied due to their applications in communication theory, cryptography, and combinatorics. Recently, geometric interpretations have provided new insights into intersecting codes, both in the Hamming metric and, more recently, in the rank metric for linear codes. In this paper, we introduce and study matrix rank-metric intersecting codes. By defining the support of a matrix as its row space, we extend the notion of intersecting codes to the matrix rank-metric setting. Using the slice space associated with the generator tensor of a rank-metric code, we derive a geometric characterization that is equivalent to the intersecting property. This characterization generalizes the known results for linear rank-metric intersecting codes and highlights both analogies and differences with the linear case. In particular, it yields bounds on the parameters of intersecting codes, one of which is sharp and differs from the one in the linear case, together with first constructions. We then consider codes that are closed under multiplication, i.e. matrix algebras. In this setting, the intersecting property can be read off from the algebraic structure, namely the Jacobson radical and the socle. This provides a simple and flexible way to construct many intersecting codes, including codes that do not satisfy the classical sufficient condition on the minimum distance.

title: Plotkin-optimal pure quantum LRCs with large minimum distances from NMDS codes
summary: Quantum locally recoverable codes (qLRCs) are a class of quantum error-correcting codes that can recover an erased qudit by accessing only a few other qudits. This paper develops a general framework for constructing optimal pure qLRCs that attain the Plotkin-like bound, referred to as Plotkin-optimal pure qLRCs, from Hermitian dual-containing near maximum-distance separable (NMDS) codes. Focusing on a special class of NMDS codes called extended subcodes of generalized Reed-Solomon (ESGRS) codes, we determine their localities by analyzing certain subset sum problems over finite fields. By further exploiting the algebraic structures of ESGRS codes and related codes, we construct four families of Plotkin-optimal pure qLRCs with large lengths and more flexible minimum distances than existing constructions. These constructions provide strong global error-correction capability while retaining local recovery. To the best of our knowledge, they give the first families of qLRCs attaining the pure Plotkin-like bound. In addition, by using the resulting locality property, we resolve in the negative a related problem on ESGRS codes supporting combinatorial designs.

AI.tldr: 该文提出从Hermitian对偶包含的NMDS码（特别是ESGRS码）构造达到Plotkin型界的纯量子局部可恢复码（qLRCs）的一般框架，并给出四类新构造。
